package_info.package_versions: Malicious versions published May 21-22, 2022 (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was hijacked via account takeover and injected with code that exfiltrates all environment variables—including AWS credentials—to an external attacker-controlled server.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects all environment variables and sends them via HTTP POST to anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating all environment variables to an external server is a clear sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate package should not access or transmit environment variables, especially not to an external domain.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Diagnostics tools may collect environment variables for local debugging, but never transmit them externally without user consent.
key_indicators: Network request to external, non-official domain

attack_chain.action: Attacker takes over the PyPI account and publishes a new version of ctx with malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to users via PyPI.

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the ctx package, triggering the malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Environment variables are collected and exfiltrated.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code sends all environment variables (including AWS credentials) to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive credentials for further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Import-time or install-time network requests to untrusted domains
Access to all environment variables in package initialization code
Exfiltration of environment data via HTTP POST
file_indicators: ctx/__init__.py or main module containing os.environ and requests.post
network_indicators: Unusual outbound HTTP POST requests during package import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that access environment variables and make outbound network requests during import or installation. Flag any code that sends environment data to non-official domains, especially during package initialization. Use static analysis to detect os.environ or similar calls combined with network functions in package entry points.
